chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abd Allah ibn Bukayr, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). A messenger of his uncle, Abd Allah ibn Ali, came to him and said to him: Your uncle says to you, 'We sought the Aqeeqa (sacrificial animal for a newborn), but we did not find it, so what do you think? Should we give in charity the price of it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No. Indeed, Allah loves the feeding of the food and the shedding of the blood.'

key_terms.إِرَاقَة: Iraqah: The act of shedding or pouring out (specifically blood in ritual context)
key_terms.الدِّمَاء: Ad-dima': The blood (of the sacrificial animal)
key_terms.الْعَقِيقَة: Aqeeqa: The sacrificial animal slaughtered on the occasion of a child's birth

ai.seo_question: Can the price of the Aqeeqa animal be given as charity instead of sacrificing the animal?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the Aqeeqa is a specific ritual act (fi'l) rather than a general charitable gift, requiring the actual slaughter and consumption of the animal's meat. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly view that the spiritual merit lies in the physical performance of the sacrifice and the communal sharing of its meat, distinguishing it from the monetary compensation (fidya) used in other contexts like Hajj or fasting.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abdullah Bin Bukeyr who said,

‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullahasws, so there came a messenger of hisasws uncle Abdullah Bin Ali, so he said, ‘Your uncle is saying to youasws, ‘We sought the Aqeeqa, but we did not find it, so what is yourasws view, should we give in charity with its price?’ So heasws said: ‘No! Allahazwjsaww Loves feeding of the food, and outpouring of the blood (of the sacrificial animal)’.
en.sarwar: 6. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from ‘Abd Allah ibn Bukayr who has said the following:

“Once I was with abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when a messenger from his uncle came and said, ‘Your uncle says, “We tried to find ‘Aqiqah but could not find one. Do you think our giving its price in charity is sufficient?”’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No, Allah loves feeding of food and slaughtering animals (to feeding the needy).”’
